title: Expose more complete set of arguments to screenshot_pdf
description:
First, I used Claude to walk through generating this pull request, so sincere apologies if I've used that tool in a way here that isn't helpful.

The root issue I started with is that when saving gt tables to PDF things like `data_color` and `cell_fill` are not shown in the PDF ([#1502](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1502) & [#1041](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1041)). The reason appears to be that the `print_background` argument cannot be set to TRUE because it is not exposed in `screenshot_pdf` and instead is always the default FALSE. There are existing webshot2 issues mentioning the absence of this argument and others ([#11](https://github.com/rstudio/webshot2/issues/11) & [#50](https://github.com/rstudio/webshot2/issues/50)).

In the past I've worked around this limitation in gt by creating my own custom `gtsave` function that calls the chromote functions directly in order to pass other arguments.

The only change here should be the addition of several PDF specific arguments, including one for `print_background`.

title: fix: Set device width and height before screenshot
description:
We've noticed, e.g. in rstudio/chromote#197, that for Chrome's new headless mode (v132+), `ChromoteSession$new()` and `ChromoteSession$new_session()` with `width` and `height` don't actually set the viewport width and height.

This PR works around that limitation by calling `Emulation$setDeviceMetricsOverride()` before taking the screenshot.

Fixes rstudio/chromote#197

title: feat(webshot): Round v{width,height} to nearest integer
description:
For rstudio/chromote#183

Chrome expects integer values for `vwidth` and `vheight`, so `webshot()` now rounds to these values to the nearest integer. If this behavior is somehow problematic, you can use `vwidth = I(my_width)` to avoid the conversion.

title: fix(webshot): Rethrow underlying chromote errors
description:
For rstudio/chromote#183

Prior to this PR we could call `s$close()` even if `s` is `NULL` because the session wasn't started correctly. We also didn't have a `catch()` in the promise chain, which would cause `webshot()` to swallow uncaught errors.

title: If the file contains backslashes, it will create an invalid file URL.
description: This issue https://github.com/dmurdoch/rgl/issues/391 was due to `webshot2::webshot` receiving `tempfile(ext = ".html")` as the `url` argument.  It recognized it as a file, and called `file_url(url)`, but didn't fix the backslashes, so it created an invalid URL.  This PR fixes that problem.

Add `use_srgb_color_profile` argument to increase portability of screenshots
description:
By default, chromote will mirror the color profile of the main monitor of the machine used to take the screenshot. This means that screenshots taken on a laptop plugged into an external monitor will often have subtly different colors than one taken when the laptop is using its built-in monitor. This problem will be even more likely across machines.

To remedy this we set the [Chrome headless argument `force-color-profile`](https://peter.sh/experiments/chromium-command-line-switches/#force-color-profile) to `"srgb"` so the color profile used is always the same across machines/monitors. 

The `use_srgb_color_profile` argument defaults to `TRUE`. This may break visual tests that use `webshot()` output but I think it's ultimately a better default than the non-portable mirroring of the current monitor's profile.

title: Fix lockup
description: This PR fixes the lockup described in https://github.com/rstudio/chromote/issues/48  when taking a webshot.  It puts the wait for the loadEvent in place before navigating to the page, but does it asynchronously.  I think when it was put in place after, it could be called too late, after the event had been missed.

title: Maybe a bug fix for lockups
description:
In https://github.com/rstudio/chromote/issues/48 I described lockups that happen in `chromote` when using `webshot2`.  I narrowed the issue down to the section of code modified in this PR, and thought the code looked wrong.  This PR appears to fix the issue, but honestly I don't understand async programming well enough to know if it's right.

The idea is that one `then()` clause contained these two lines:

```
s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE)
s$Page$loadEventFired(wait_ = FALSE)
```

which I suppose are both supposed to complete before we move on.  The change is to group them into one object using

```
c(s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE),
    s$Page$loadEventFired(wait_ = FALSE))
```

in the hope that this makes `promises` wait for both to complete.  And it seems to work!

title: Correct order of parameters for cliprect
description:
Great packages, thank you!

It seems that the order of the parameters of cliprect is not the same for webshot and webshot2:

Here top is clipped by 100:

`webshot::webshot("https://cran.r-project.org/", cliprect = c(100, 0, 300, 300), file = "webshot.png")`

![webshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14161912/70647546-2b082100-1c17-11ea-920d-87b9c7cb4b66.png)

Here left is clipped by 100:

`webshot2::webshot("https://cran.r-project.org/", cliprect = c(100, 0, 300, 300), file="webshot2.png")`

![webshot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14161912/70647568-38251000-1c17-11ea-9ac2-e1c7838ff53c.png)

I updated the documentation to reflect this difference.
